modernText: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
message: Sometimes the bravest thing in the chaos is to stop fighting every front at once and let something else hold the line for a minute.

body: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
modernText: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
message: The math never works out. All that height of worry, and not a single inch of it ever came back as help.

body: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
modernText: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
message: A gentle nudge to notice when the weight of it all is quietly flattening you, before it becomes the whole day.

body: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
modernText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
message: Let peace be the thing that referees the noise, the voice that gets the final call when everything is shouting at once.

body: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
modernText: Commit your way to Yahweh. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
message: Committing the way doesn't mean controlling it. It's loosening the grip on the parts that were never yours to hold anyway.

body: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
modernText: Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
message: Rest and wait are hard verbs when you're wired to fix. This is permission to stop performing calm and actually have some.

body: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
modernText: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
message: It doesn't say you'll skip the hard water. It says you won't go under in it, and you won't go through it alone.

body: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
modernText: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
message: On a day this heavy, this is the quiet reminder that you're known, not just by the stress but by something that holds you in it.

body: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
modernText: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
message: Hard to imagine being delighted in when you feel like a mess. This says you are, exactly as frayed as you are right now.

body: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
modernText: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
message: A place to sit down in the middle of the storm. Not a fix for the weather, a shelter while it passes.

body: I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
modernText: I will say of Yahweh, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
message: Saying it out loud, refuge, even when it doesn't feel true yet. Sometimes steadiness starts as something you choose to lean on.

body: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
message: Strong and courageous, and then the real reason: not because you've got it, but because you're not facing it by yourself.

body: And David said to Solomon his son, Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the LORD God, even my God, will be with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, until thou hast finished all the work for the service of the house of the LORD.
modernText: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed; for Yahweh God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you, nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of Yahweh’s house is finished.
message: A big task, a tired person, and the same quiet promise underneath it: you won't be left to finish it alone.

body: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
modernText: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
message: When the fear has a dozen faces today, this asks a steadying question back: if you're held, then of what, exactly, are you afraid?

body: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.
modernText: Wait for Yahweh. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for Yahweh.
message: Wait is the hardest instruction when you're wired to act. This makes waiting itself an act of strength, not a failure to move.

body: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
modernText: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.
message: The soul quietly waiting, not because nothing's wrong, but because it's found something steadier than solving everything to rest on.

body: It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
modernText: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
message: Even hoping quietly counts as doing something. Sometimes the steadiest move is to wait without forcing the fix.

body: The LORD God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments.
modernText: Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
message: Steady feet on uneven ground. Not the terrain getting easier, just a surer footing given for the climb.

body: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
modernText: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
message: The drawing-near goes both ways. Take one small step toward steadier ground and find it was already moving toward you.

body: I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
modernText: I have set Yahweh always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
message: Keeping something steady in your line of sight so the shaking doesn't get the last word on how the day goes.

body: Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength:
modernText: Trust in Yahweh forever; for in Yah, Yahweh, is an everlasting Rock.
message: Everlasting strength, the kind that doesn't run out mid-week. Something to lean the whole weight of a hard day against.

body: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
modernText: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
message: Peace as a settled fact, not a mood you have to manufacture. Something already true underneath however today feels.

body: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
modernText: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
message: For the kind of tired that comes from doing the right things with no payoff in sight. A quiet nudge to not give out just yet.

body: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
modernText: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
message: Specifically for the empty tank. Strength offered to the exact people who feel like they have none left to give.

body: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
modernText: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
message: Not a promise you'll stop being tired, but that the running won't be fueled by you alone. Something gets renewed that you didn't manufacture.

body: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
modernText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
message: Before anything gets fixed, there's comfort. The kind that meets you in the stress instead of waiting for you to be past it.

body: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
modernText: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.
message: The verse for when your body is in bed but your brain is still at the office. Rest offered not because everything's handled, but because you're held.

body: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
modernText: I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahweh sustains me.
message: You made it to morning. Not because you white-knuckled through the night, but because something steadier than you kept watch.

body: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
modernText: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
message: Even walking straight through the worst of it, the promise isn't 'no shadow.' It's 'not alone in the shadow.'

body: I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
modernText: I sought Yahweh, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
message: Not just the big fears, all of them. The low-grade background dread you forgot you were even carrying.

body: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
modernText: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
message: It doesn't pretend you won't be afraid. It just gives you somewhere to put the fear when you are.

body: In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.
modernText: In God, I praise his word. In God, I put my trust. I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
message: What can flesh really do next to the thing holding you. A quiet resizing of what felt enormous a second ago.

body: I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.
modernText: Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.
message: Called out of the tight, pressed-in place and given room to breathe. Sometimes the answer to stress is just space.

body: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?
modernText: Yahweh is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
message: If help is actually on your side, the list of things to brace against gets a lot shorter.

body: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
modernText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
message: When your heart is overwhelmed is literally the condition this was written for. Led up to something higher and steadier than where you're standing.

body: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.
modernText: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
message: A morning ask: let me hear something kind before the day starts talking. Point me somewhere before the noise does.

body: He shall not be afraid of evil tidings: his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD.
modernText: He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Yahweh.
message: For the person bracing for the next notification. A steadiness that doesn't flinch every time the phone buzzes.

body: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
modernText: Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me.
message: Not lifted out of the trouble, revived in the middle of walking through it. Kept moving when you thought you were out of gas.

body: Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
modernText: Therefore we won’t be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas;
message: Even if the ground itself moved, the verse says we won't fear. A stubborn calm that doesn't depend on things staying put.

body: Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.
modernText: though its waters roar and are troubled, though the mountains tremble with their swelling.
message: Let the waters roar. The point isn't that it gets quiet, it's that something stays unmoved while it's loud.

body: When I said, My foot slippeth; thy mercy, O LORD, held me up.
modernText: When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, Yahweh, held me up.
message: That moment you felt yourself going under, and something caught you. Mercy showing up right at the slip.

body: The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.
modernText: Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.
message: Preserved, kept, watched. Steady words for a mind that's been running worst-case scenarios all day.

body: The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
modernText: Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
message: The ordinary comings and goings, the commute, the errands, the whole anxious day, all of it watched over.

body: For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.
modernText: For I, Yahweh your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’
message: A hand actually taking yours. Not a pep talk from across the room, closer than that.

body: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
modernText: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
message: Called by name, claimed. On a day you feel like a number on everyone's to-do list, you're known by yours.

body: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.
modernText: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
message: Even if the solid things shift, the kindness doesn't. Something that outlasts what you thought was permanent.

body: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.
modernText: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
message: Real peace isn't the loud kind that performs calm. It's quiet, and it just stays.

body: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the LORD JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
modernText: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”
message: Saying it out loud, I will trust and not be afraid, even before the feeling catches up. Sometimes steadiness starts as a sentence.

body: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
modernText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
message: When your own head runs nothing but worst cases, this says the thoughts toward you are peace. A kinder narrator than the one you've been listening to.

body: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is.
modernText: “Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh.
message: Blessed is the one who leans their weight somewhere steadier than their own planning. Permission to stop being your own foundation.

body: For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
modernText: For he will be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green, and will not be concerned in the year of drought. It won’t cease from yielding fruit.
message: Roots down by the water, so the heat comes and the leaf stays green. Steadiness that doesn't depend on the conditions being good.

body: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
modernText: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
message: An old way of saying stop borrowing tomorrow's panic. Your life is more than the list you're stressing over.

body: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
modernText: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
message: The birds aren't out there spiraling about provision, and they're fine. A nudge that you might be more cared for than the anxiety suggests.

body: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
modernText: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
message: One thing to orient around instead of twenty. When everything feels urgent, this quietly reorders the pile.

body: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
modernText: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
message: Said to people in an actual sinking boat. Not a dismissal of the storm, a question about who's in it with them.

body: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
modernText: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
message: Three words to a storm: peace, be still. For the internal weather too, not just the lake.

body: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
modernText: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
message: Right after the worst news, this. Not 'it's fine,' just 'don't do this part alone, and keep holding on.'

body: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
modernText: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
message: It's honest: in the world you'll have trouble. The peace isn't instead of the trouble, it's underneath it.

body: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
modernText: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
message: Where your mind lives changes how the day feels. A quiet suggestion about where to let it rest.

body: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
modernText: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
message: Persuaded that not one thing on the whole list, not the future, not the 3am fear, can cut you off from the love holding you.

body: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
modernText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
message: Nothing in all creation. The verse runs out of categories before it finds one that can separate you from it.

body: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
modernText: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
message: Whatever's pressing in isn't unprecedented, and it isn't a sealed room. There's always a door, even when you can't see it yet.

body: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
modernText: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
message: Pressed on every side but not crushed. Honest about the pressure, stubborn about the not-crushed part.

body: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
modernText: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
message: The grace doesn't wait for you to get strong. It shows up in the depleted, running-on-fumes version of you.

body: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;
modernText: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
message: Strength on the inside, where the stress actually lives. Not just powering through, being reinforced underneath.

body: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
modernText: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
message: Not a hype slogan. A quiet 'you're not drawing on your own tank for this' on a day the tank is empty.

body: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
modernText: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
message: Need, not every want. A promise sized to what the day actually requires, which is usually less than the anxiety insists.

body: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
modernText: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
message: When every small thing feels huge, this lifts your eyes for a second. Not to dismiss it, to resize it.

body: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
modernText: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
message: Everlasting comfort and good hope, already given. Not earned by holding it together, just given.

body: Comfort your hearts, and stablish you in every good word and work.
modernText: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.
message: Comfort your heart and steady you. The two things the stress has been quietly chipping at, named and addressed.

body: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
message: I will never leave thee. On a day everyone needs something and no one's got you, this says someone does, and isn't going anywhere.

body: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
modernText: So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
message: A helper on your side changes the math on fear. You can say 'I will not fear' and actually mean it.

body: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
modernText: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
message: Lay aside the weight, the verse says, like it's a thing you're allowed to set down. Not every weight is yours to run with.

body: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
modernText: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
message: One steady thing to keep your eyes on while you run, so the chaos in your peripheral vision stops setting the pace.

body: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
modernText: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
message: Letting go of needing to force the outcome. Trusting the timing to something that isn't panicking the way you are.

body: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.
modernText: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
message: After the hard stretch, not a vague 'it gets better,' but settled, strengthened, steadied. The after is part of the promise.

body: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:
modernText: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
message: The anxious thoughts you can't even organize, this invites them to be seen instead of hidden. Known all the way down, mess included.

body: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
modernText: See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
message: After the searching, a gentle leading. Not judged for what's in there, guided through it.

body: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.
modernText: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don’t fret; it leads only to evildoing.
message: Fret not is a tall order, so read it as permission more than command. The fretting was never the thing holding your life together anyway.

body: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.
modernText: I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.
message: That exact fantasy of just disappearing somewhere quiet, the Bible has it too. You're not weak for wishing you could fly away from it for a while.

body: He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
modernText: He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken.
message: Not 'never moved,' just 'not greatly moved.' Room to be shaken without being toppled.

body: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
modernText: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
message: Pointing your expectation at something steadier than outcomes you can't control. A quieter place to hang your hope.

body: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
modernText: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us.
message: Pour out your heart, it says, not tidy it up first. You can bring the unfiltered version here.

body: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
modernText: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
message: Honest about the failing part, your body and your nerve giving out, and just as honest about the strength that isn't yours to run out of.

body: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.
modernText: In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.
message: For the specific day, not trouble in general. This one, the one you're actually in, is the one it says gets answered.

body: Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.
modernText: Return to your rest, my soul, for Yahweh has dealt bountifully with you.
message: Talking to your own soul like a friend: come back, you can rest now. Sometimes you have to tell yourself the thing you'd tell anyone else.

body: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.
modernText: Those who love your law have great peace. Nothing causes them to stumble.
message: A peace big enough that the small things stop snagging you. Less flinching at every little thing that goes sideways.

body: They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.
modernText: Those who trust in Yahweh are as Mount Zion, which can’t be moved, but remains forever.
message: Trust that makes you harder to move, not because nothing pushes, but because of what you're anchored to.

body: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.
modernText: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
message: The verse that basically calls out hustle culture. Staying up late grinding isn't the thing holding it together, and rest is actually given to you.

body: Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
modernText: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
message: A soul calmed like a kid who's done crying and just rests against someone. Not fixed, just quiet and held.

body: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.
modernText: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.
message: Right when your spirit is overwhelmed, the verse says the path is still known, by someone who isn't overwhelmed with you.

body: The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.
modernText: Yahweh upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down.
message: For everyone currently bent under the weight. Upheld and raised, specifically the ones who feel like they're going down.

body: The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
modernText: Yahweh is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.
message: A pile-up of steady words, rock, fortress, deliverer, like the verse itself is bracing you with everything it's got.

body: Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah.
modernText: You are my hiding place. You will preserve me from trouble. You will surround me with songs of deliverance.
message: A hiding place isn't avoidance, it's a breather. Somewhere to be surrounded by something other than the trouble for a minute.

body: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
modernText: The righteous cry, and Yahweh hears, and delivers them out of all their troubles.
message: The crying out gets heard. Not performance, not composure, just the cry, and it reaches someone.

body: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.
modernText: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but Yahweh delivers him out of them all.
message: It doesn't lowball it: many afflictions. And it doesn't lowball the other side either: out of them all.

body: I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
modernText: I waited patiently for Yahweh. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
message: Waiting and being heard in the same breath. The patience wasn't wasted, something was listening the whole time.

body: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
modernText: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.
message: Brought up out of the sinking place and set on something that holds. The after-picture for the part that feels like quicksand.

body: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
modernText: Yahweh will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.
message: A refuge specifically in the times of trouble, not just the calm stretches. Built for exactly now.

body: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
modernText: Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”
message: An open invitation with your name on it: call, in the trouble, and be answered. You don't have to earn the right to.

body: LORD, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought all our works in us.
modernText: Yahweh, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also done all our work for us.
message: Peace as something ordained, arranged, set up on purpose for you. Not a fluke you have to hope for.

body: Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the LORD, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
modernText: Don’t be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you,” says Yahweh. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
message: Even calling you small, it turns straight to help. Being little here isn't a disqualifier, it's the reason help shows up.

body: Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west;
modernText: Don’t be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east, and gather you from the west.
message: The whole weight of it sits on one phrase: I am with thee. The fear shrinks next to the company.

body: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
modernText: Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
message: Carried the whole way, even to gray hair. On a day you feel like you're hauling yourself, this says you're the one being carried.

body: And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
modernText: and Yahweh will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail.
message: Guided continually, and watered even in the dry stretch. Provision that doesn't wait for conditions to improve.

body: The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: and he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee; and shall say, Destroy them.
modernText: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, ‘Destroy!’
message: However far you feel like you're falling, the verse says there's a floor, and it's arms. Underneath, always underneath.

body: Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.
modernText: But as for me, I will look to Yahweh. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
message: Looking up and waiting, even when nothing's answered yet, because the hearing is already a given.

body: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
modernText: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
message: You're not used up, not finished, not past the point of mercy. The supply hasn't run out, even today.

body: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
modernText: They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
message: Whatever you spent yesterday, the mercy resets overnight. You don't start today already in the red.

body: And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the LORD unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
modernText: and he said, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, king Jehoshaphat. Yahweh says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
message: The one that quietly takes the weight off: this isn't yours to win alone. The battle has a different owner.

body: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you.
modernText: You will not need to fight this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Go out against them tomorrow, for Yahweh is with you.’ ”
message: Permission to stop swinging at every front. Sometimes standing still is the strategy, not the surrender.

body: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our LORD: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
modernText: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.”
message: On an empty day, this points to a strength that isn't manufactured by your mood. Joy as a source, not just a feeling.

body: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
modernText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
message: A specific promise for the part of stress that steals sleep: you'll lie down, and it'll actually be rest.

body: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.
modernText: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
message: It names how heaviness literally bends you, and how small a thing can lift it. One good word can do more than you'd think.

body: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
modernText: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.
message: Hand over the doing, and the thinking steadies. The spiraling often settles once the grip on outcomes loosens.

body: The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
modernText: Yahweh’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
message: Somewhere to run that's actually safe, not just a distraction. A tower, not a hiding-from.

body: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
modernText: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.
message: A lot of the stress is just the fear of what people think. This quietly unhooks you from that trap.

body: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
modernText: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
message: Said the night before the worst day. Not 'nothing's wrong,' just 'don't let the trouble have your whole heart.'

body: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
modernText: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
message: A promise not to be left alone in it. Comfort coming to you, not you having to go find it.

body: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
modernText: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
message: The rest offered here is soul-deep, not just a day off. The kind that reaches the part of you that's actually tired.

body: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
modernText: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
message: Not a promise of no load, a promise of a lighter one, shared. The weight redistributed so it stops crushing.

body: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:
modernText: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
message: Named gently, by name, while mid-spiral over the many things. Seen in the exact overwhelm, not scolded for it.

body: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
modernText: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
message: One thing needful, out of the twenty that feel urgent. Permission to let most of the list be optional for a minute.

body: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
modernText: Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
message: Contentment learned, not faked, even in the hard state. Something steadier than circumstances deciding how you feel.

body: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
modernText: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
message: When you don't even have words for the stress, this says the praying gets done for you. You don't have to articulate it right.

body: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
modernText: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
message: Comfort in all of it, no tribulation too small or too big to qualify. And later, that comfort becomes something you can pass on.

body: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
modernText: Yahweh, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
message: A morning habit for an anxious mind: say it before you scroll, look up before the day starts talking.

body: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
modernText: Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings,
message: Kept as close as the thing you'd instinctively protect, tucked under a wing. Precious, not a burden.

body: The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;
modernText: May Yahweh answer you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high,
message: A blessing spoken over you for the hard day: may you be heard, may the name hold you.

body: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
modernText: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of Yahweh our God.
message: Everyone leans on something. This gently asks what you've been bracing against the stress with, and offers something steadier.

body: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.
modernText: The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses.
message: Honest that the troubles feel bigger than usual, and it doesn't argue. It just asks to be brought out, and trusts the answer.

body: For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me; he shall set me up upon a rock.
modernText: For in the day of trouble, he will keep me secretly in his pavilion. In the secret place of his tabernacle, he will hide me. He will lift me up on a rock.
message: A tent to be tucked into when it's too much out there. Shelter, not a lecture about toughing it out.

body: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.
modernText: Yahweh is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him.
message: Strength and a shield, and then the relief in the next line: my heart trusted, and I was helped. The trusting led somewhere.

body: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
modernText: For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
message: It doesn't deny the night of it. It just says the night isn't the whole story, and morning is coming.

body: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the LORD.
modernText: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in Yahweh.
message: Addressed to everyone still hoping, even faintly. Courage offered specifically to the ones hanging on.

body: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.
modernText: Our soul has waited for Yahweh. He is our help and our shield.
message: Waiting, not idly, but like watching for someone who's actually coming. Help and cover on the way.

body: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.
modernText: A man’s steps are established by Yahweh. He delights in his way.
message: On a day the path feels random and overwhelming, this says the steps are ordered. You're not just wandering through it.

body: Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.
modernText: Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahweh holds him up with his hand.
message: It allows for the fall. It just says the fall isn't final, because of whose hand is holding yours.

body: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
modernText: God is within her. She shall not be moved. God will help her at dawn.
message: The steadiness isn't out at the edges, it's right in the middle of you. Held from the center, not just the outside.

body: Behold, God is mine helper: the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.
modernText: Behold, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my soul.
message: Four plain words for a day you feel unsupported: God is mine helper. Said flatly, like a fact to lean on.

body: Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.
modernText: Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.
message: Shelter until it passes. Not a promise it won't rain, a promise of a dry place while it does.

body: Because thou hast been my help, therefore in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
modernText: For you have been my help. I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
message: From under the wing, there's even room to be glad. Shelter that isn't just surviving, it can hum a little.

body: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
modernText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation.
message: The opposite inventory from the one your stress keeps. A quiet suggestion that you're being given to, daily, under all the noise.

body: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them.
modernText: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, who have set their hearts on a pilgrimage.
message: Blessed is the one whose strength isn't self-generated. Permission to stop being your own power source.

body: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
modernText: He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.
message: A soft image for a hard day: covered with feathers, tucked under a wing. Safety that feels gentle, not armored.

body: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;
modernText: You shall not be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day,
message: For the fears that get loud after dark. The verse names the night specifically, because it knows that's when it spirals.

body: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him.
modernText: Like a father has compassion on his children, so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.
message: Not disappointed in you for struggling. Looked at the way a parent looks at a kid who's had a hard day, with tenderness.

body: For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
modernText: For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.
message: He knows you're dust, that you're not built to carry all of it. Your limits aren't a failing, they're understood.

body: Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses.
modernText: Then they cry to Yahweh in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress.
message: A pattern repeated all through this psalm: they cried, and were brought out. The crying is enough to start it.

body: He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.
modernText: He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still.
message: The storm doesn't have to be fought into submission. It can simply be made calm, by someone who isn't rattled by it.

body: Ye that fear the LORD, trust in the LORD: he is their help and their shield.
modernText: You who fear Yahweh, trust in Yahweh! He is their help and their shield.
message: Help and shield again, because you probably need to hear it more than once on a day like this.

body: The LORD is my strength and song, and is become my salvation.
modernText: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation.
message: Strength and song in the same breath, because sometimes steadiness sounds like finally being able to exhale.

body: My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.
modernText: My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to your word.
message: It names the exact feeling, your soul melting under the weight, and asks plainly for strength. No pretending required.

body: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word.
modernText: You are my hiding place and my shield. I hope in your word.
message: A place to disappear for a minute and something to stand behind. Both, for a day coming at you from every side.

body: Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me: yet thy commandments are my delights.
modernText: Trouble and anguish have taken hold of me. Your commandments are my delight.
message: Honest that trouble has taken hold, and stubborn that there's still something good to hold onto inside it.

body: In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.
modernText: In my distress, I cried to Yahweh. He answered me.
message: Short and settled: I cried in the distress, and I was heard. Past tense, like it's already been proven once.

body: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.
modernText: In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.
message: Answered and strengthened on the same day you cried. The strength came with the answer, not after you earned it.

body: For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
modernText: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
message: A shelter built for the ones with nothing left, from the storm and the heat both. Refuge sized for empty.

body: O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
modernText: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
message: A morning ask for strength that isn't yours: be our arm today. Borrowed strength, requested daily.

body: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.
modernText: Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong! Don’t be afraid! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
message: Spoken straight to the fearful heart, not the brave one. The encouragement is aimed exactly where the fear lives.

body: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding.
modernText: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
message: You're tired because you're human. The one holding it all isn't, and never runs down, even when you do.

body: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
modernText: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
message: When there's no visible path through the stress, this says a way gets made. Not found, made, where there wasn't one.

body: I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass;
modernText: “I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass?
message: The comfort is personal and repeated, I, even I. Not a system, someone, leaning in to steady you.

body: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.
modernText: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.”
message: For the soul that's running on empty, this promises it gets filled, not just propped up. The weary part, specifically, satisfied.

body: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
modernText: “Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm. There is nothing too hard for you.
message: Whatever's looming too big to solve, this quietly resizes it. Nothing on your list is in the too-hard category for the one you're handing it to.

body: Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:
modernText: For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls:
message: A verse that lists everything going wrong, the whole harvest failing, and still turns toward trust. Honest about the lack first.

body: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
modernText: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
message: The 'yet' doing all the work. Not because things are fine, but because there's something to stand on that the failures can't touch.

body: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
modernText: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, “This is Yahweh’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says Yahweh of Armies.
message: Permission to stop forcing it with sheer effort. The thing you're grinding at isn't actually powered by how hard you push.

body: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
modernText: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
message: The needs you're anxiously tracking are already known. You're not the only one keeping the list.

body: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
modernText: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
message: The last thing said before leaving, and it's a promise not to actually leave. Always, including this exact stressed-out moment.

body: Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be likeminded one toward another according to Christ Jesus:
modernText: Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,
message: Named as the God of patience, so you can borrow some when yours is gone, and of consolation, for when you need that too.

body: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
modernText: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
message: The chaos in your head isn't coming from the steady place. Peace is the native language there, not the noise.

body: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
modernText: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
message: Whatever's unfinished and stressing you, this says the finishing isn't all on you. Something committed to seeing it through.

body: For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.
modernText: For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
message: Not 'I know how this works out,' but 'I know who's holding it.' Certainty about the person, not the outcome.

body: Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.
modernText: Therefore let them also who suffer according to the will of God in doing good entrust their souls to him, as to a faithful Creator.
message: Hand the keeping of you over to someone faithful, and get back to just living the day. You don't have to guard yourself every second.

body: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
modernText: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
message: Fear and this kind of love can't fully share a room. The more one fills the space, the less oxygen the other has.

body: But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
modernText: But you, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
message: A shield around you and a hand lifting your head when it's hung low. Both at once, for a day that's got you staring at the floor.

body: Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
modernText: Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. Give me relief from my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer.
message: Given room when things felt tight. The verse remembers being boxed in, then suddenly able to breathe again.

body: But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.
modernText: But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation.
message: After a whole psalm of 'how long,' it lands here: I have trusted in thy mercy. Trust chosen, not felt, and that still counts.

body: Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.
modernText: Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in you.
message: A short, plain ask for a shaky day: keep me. Sometimes the only prayer you've got is 'hold onto me,' and that's enough.

body: It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.
modernText: the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect?
message: Strength handed to you like something strapped on, and the path smoothed. Equipped for the thing you feel unready for.

body: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy right hand hath holden me up, and thy gentleness hath made me great.
modernText: You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your right hand sustains me. Your gentleness has made me great.
message: Not toughness, gentleness, is what it credits. You might be steadier than you think, and from a softer source than you'd expect.

body: But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me.
modernText: But don’t be far off, Yahweh. You are my help. Hurry to help me!
message: Permission to pray urgently. Don't be far, hurry, is a completely acceptable thing to say when it's a lot.

body: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
modernText: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
message: Goodness and mercy following you around like they're assigned to you. Even on a hard day, they're still trailing behind, keeping up.

body: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.
modernText: Though an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I will be confident.
message: Even surrounded, the heart doesn't have to fear. Not because the threat is small, but because of who's standing with you in it.

body: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
modernText: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.
message: An honest admission: I'd have given out, if I hadn't held onto the hope of seeing goodness again. The believing is what kept you standing.

body: For thou art my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy name’s sake lead me, and guide me.
modernText: For you are my rock and my fortress, therefore for your name’s sake lead me and guide me.
message: Rock, fortress, and then: lead me. Steadiness and direction from the same place, for when you feel both shaky and lost.

body: I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy: for thou hast considered my trouble; thou hast known my soul in adversities;
modernText: I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
message: Known, specifically in the hard times. Not just when you're fine, your soul is seen in the adversity itself.

body: My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.
modernText: My times are in your hand. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from those who persecute me.
message: The timing you can't control, the waiting, the when, all held in a steadier hand than yours. You can loosen the grip on the clock.

body: The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
modernText: Yahweh’s angel encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
message: A quiet image of being surrounded, not by threats, by protection. Camped around you while you sleep through the stress.

body: Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.
modernText: Trust in Yahweh, and do good. Dwell in the land, and enjoy safe pasture.
message: Trust, do the next good thing, and provision follows. Permission to stop solving the whole future and just do today's small right thing.

body: Delight thyself also in the LORD: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
modernText: Also delight yourself in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
message: When stress has crowded out everything you actually enjoy, this points back toward delight. The heart gets tended to, not just the task list.

body: But the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD: he is their strength in the time of trouble.
modernText: But the salvation of the righteous is from Yahweh. He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.
message: Strength that shows up on schedule, in the time of trouble, not a general reserve but a specific delivery for now.

body: The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing: thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness.
modernText: Yahweh will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness.
message: For the days you can barely get up, this meets you on the bed, in the languishing. Strength brought to where you are, not demanded of you.

body: Yet the LORD will command his lovingkindness in the day time, and in the night his song shall be with me, and my prayer unto the God of my life.
modernText: Yahweh will command his loving kindness in the daytime. In the night his song shall be with me: a prayer to the God of my life.
message: A kindness scheduled for the day and a song for the night. Both halves of a hard 24 hours accounted for.

body: Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.
modernText: Evening, morning, and at noon, I will cry out in distress. He will hear my voice.
message: Permission to keep coming back, all day, as many times as the anxiety spikes. There's no quota on how often you're allowed to reach out.

body: But I will sing of thy power; yea, I will sing aloud of thy mercy in the morning: for thou hast been my defence and refuge in the day of my trouble.
modernText: But I will sing of your strength. Yes, I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning. For you have been my high tower, a refuge in the day of my distress.
message: Something worth singing about even mid-trouble: a defence that holds, a refuge that's open, on the exact day you need it.

body: For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.
modernText: For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower from the enemy.
message: Already proven, past tense: thou hast been a shelter. Not a maybe, a track record you can lean on again.

body: Be thou my strong habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: thou hast given commandment to save me; for thou art my rock and my fortress.
modernText: Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may always go. Give the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
message: A place you can go back to as often as you need. Not a one-time rescue, a standing invitation to return.

body: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: my sore ran in the night, and ceased not: my soul refused to be comforted.
modernText: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted.
message: It's honest about the restless kind of seeking, hands out all night, soul refusing comfort. The reaching counts even when it's desperate.

body: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
modernText: But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
message: Patient with you, not exasperated. On a day you're frustrated with yourself, the one you're reaching for is in no hurry to give up on you.

body: And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.
modernText: Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
message: A prayer for the work to hold, to mean something, to not be wasted. The effort you're pouring out, asked to be made to stick.

body: The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters, yea, than the mighty waves of the sea.
modernText: Above the voices of many waters, the mighty breakers of the sea, Yahweh on high is mighty.
message: Whatever's roaring at you, this names it as noise, and names something louder and steadier over the top of it. The waters are real, and they're not the loudest thing.

body: But the LORD is my defence; and my God is the rock of my refuge.
modernText: But Yahweh has been my high tower, my God, the rock of my refuge.
message: A defence and a rock in the same breath. For a day you feel exposed, something to both stand behind and stand on.

body: He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.
modernText: He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.
message: The prayer of the person with nothing left gets regarded, not ignored. Empty-handed isn't disqualifying here, it's the whole point.

body: Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies.
modernText: Through God, we will do valiantly. For it is he who will tread down our enemies.
message: The valiant part isn't self-generated. Through God, it says, like the courage is on loan for exactly what you're facing.

body: I love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.
modernText: I love Yahweh, because he listens to my voice, and my cries for mercy.
message: Love that grew out of being heard. Not duty, gratitude, from the simple experience of a cry that actually landed somewhere.

body: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him as long as I live.
modernText: Because he has turned his ear to me, therefore I will call on him as long as I live.
message: Because he listened once, a decision to keep coming back. The relief of knowing the line stays open for life.

body: It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in man.
modernText: It is better to take refuge in Yahweh, than to put confidence in man.
message: A quiet recalibration for when people have let you down. Somewhere steadier to put your weight than on anyone who can disappoint.

body: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.
modernText: He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.
message: The one keeping you doesn't doze off. Even when you can't hold yourself steady, the watch doesn't lapse.

body: Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
modernText: Our help is in Yahweh’s name, who made heaven and earth.
message: When you catalog where help could come from, this points past all of it to the maker of heaven and earth. Help with real backing behind it.

body: The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
modernText: Yahweh will fulfill that which concerns me. Your loving kindness, Yahweh, endures forever. Don’t forsake the works of your own hands.
message: The unfinished, worrying thing that concerns you, this says gets perfected, completed, by someone who hasn't lost track of it.

body: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
modernText: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
message: Near, specifically, to everyone who calls. Not far off and hard to reach, close, and the calling is the only requirement.

body: He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.
modernText: He will fulfill the desire of those who fear him. He also will hear their cry, and will save them.
message: The desire and the cry, both heard, both tended to. The ache under the stress isn't going unnoticed.

body: Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD his God:
modernText: Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in Yahweh, his God:
message: Happiness pinned not to circumstances but to who's helping you. A steadier foundation for a mood than how the day went.

body: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me.
modernText: Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are continually before me.
message: The opposite of forgotten. You're written on the hands of the one holding you, impossible to overlook.

body: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.
modernText: For the Lord Yahweh will help me. Therefore I have not been confounded. Therefore I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I won’t be disappointed.
message: Help, and then resolve, a face set like flint. Steadiness that comes from being backed, not from pretending you're unbothered.

body: Behold, the LORD’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear:
modernText: Behold, Yahweh’s hand is not shortened, that it can’t save; nor his ear dull, that it can’t hear.
message: If it feels like help isn't coming, this says it isn't a reach problem. The hand is long enough, the ear isn't dull.

body: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
modernText: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
message: Known down to the absurd detail, the count of your hair. If that's tracked, the things you're actually stressed about aren't slipping through unnoticed.

body: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
modernText: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
message: Called little flock, tenderly, right before 'fear not.' Small isn't a problem here, it's spoken to gently, not scolded.
